audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagree with the packet, the mirror, or their own reason. Rows 2 and 3 are labelled 'Irelia' while whys[2] ends 'genuinely even' and whys[3] ends 'a tug-of-war neither side runs away with' — packet agrees they are Skill. Rows 4, 5 and 6 are all labelled 'Skill' while the already-applied mirror audit set them to Irelia / Irelia / Dr. Mundo, and whys[6] plus the late paragraph both say he facetanks the combo and you should stop duelling.
audit.why: Levels 3-5 genuinely even out because his early sustain heals back what a clean E-Q-auto takes. Level 6 and first item are Irelia's — Blade of the Ruined King's %HP bites a health-stacker. Two tank items plus Maximum Dosage is his.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 set to Skill / Skill / Irelia / Irelia / Dr. Mundo in both layers, ratings re-scored, and report[14] corrected from 'Even' to 'Favoured' to match diff FAV.
sources: brief currentText whys[2], whys[3], whys[6], late

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why and phases[5].why were generic boilerplate, and no Dr. Mundo cooldown appeared in the full layer at all.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s and Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank — a flat 120s ult means the window never shortens as the game goes on, which is what makes the first-item all-in the right timing.
audit.corrected: The 17s and the Maximum Dosage timing written into phases[3..6].why, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup was absent from the whole page: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilizing effect that hits him, so Flawless Duet's stun is simply eaten. Also, the page says six times that Irelia's on-hit 'shreds' or 'carves' his armor/MR — Ionian Fervor is stacking attack speed plus bonus on-hit damage at max stacks and shreds no resistances at all. Heart Zapper's mechanic (it STORES a portion of the damage he takes and heals him off the burst) was never stated either, which is exactly why grinding a long trade into him fails.
audit.why: Riot's text: Mundo P — 'resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister'; Mundo W — 'storing a portion of damage he takes... he heals a percentage of the stored damage'; Mundo R — 'instantly healing a percent of his missing Health'; Irelia P — stacking Attack Speed, bonus damage on hit at max.
audit.corrected: The passive written into dosFull[2] and phases[4].why; Heart Zapper's storage into dontsFull[0].d, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns; the shred fabrication removed from whys[4], whys[5] and spikes[2].text.
sources: mirror audit drmundo__irelia point 4 and notes

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was recommended with no timing and no named source, and the boots line recommends Plated Steelcaps against a champion whose ultimate makes stacked resistances the wrong axis.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage heals a percent of his MISSING health, so Grievous Wounds applied after he casts is worth far less than Grievous Wounds applied before. Blade of the Ruined King's percent-health damage, already core in the build, is the right answer to his health stacking.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d rewritten with the missing-health mechanic and the timing; report[8] now names Maximum Dosage.
sources: enemyKit R text and percentHealth flag

notes: The packet suspectName 'Once Maximum Dosage' is a false positive — Maximum Dosage is the correct Riot name and 'Once' is just the preceding word. One departure from the packet: packet.levelChart gives first item to Skill, but the mirror audit set it to Irelia and I followed the mirror so the two directions agree; whys[5] was rewritten to match. Remaining 'shred/carve his resists' fabrications outside the length band: the mid paragraph, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[1] — worth a champion-level pass. Also live and unaddressed: nothing on the page mentions that his passive drops a cannister he can walk over to heal and cut its cooldown, which is a real denial opportunity.
